equity_bridge.item: Investments at book: equity-method 95 + equity/other securities 907 (DAZN stake received on the Foxtel sale, China investments, REA's Athena/Nexxen stakes), less ~50 for the 38% of REA-held securities belonging to minorities
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K Note 6, total 1,002 at 2026-06-30. Matching-asset rule: equity losses of affiliates (-8) and investment gains are outside Segment EBITDA, so the assets enter the bridge. Book is fair value for the quoted securities; DAZN is unquoted and carried at the fair value struck on 2025-04-02.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr on the restated continuing-operations basis (FY2023 8,012 -> FY2026 9,028), nudged up for the FY2026 run-rate (+6.8% incl. FX) and the AI-licensing and Digital Real Estate momentum; the equity CAGR is not usable as the anchor here
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (1.1% 3yr / 0.2% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (4.1%) and EPS (58%/13%). Equity is depressed by ~$850M/yr of buybacks plus dividends and by the Foxtel deconsolidation, not by weak earnings; EPS CAGRs are off a depressed FY2023 base (0.26) and FY2021 (0.56). The 5-year revenue CAGR is negative only because FY2021 (9,358) still consolidates Foxtel while FY2026 does not.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = continuing OCF - capex - SBC: FY2021 719, FY2023 658, FY2026 734 (FY2021/FY2023 OCF includes Foxtel; FY2024 and later are continuing-ops only). Owner-FCF CAGR (3.7% 3yr) exceeds reported FCF CAGR (2.9%) because SBC fell from 128 (FY2021) to 77 (FY2026) - the opposite of the usual SBC-outgrowing-cash pattern. Equity figures are total equity including NCI (CSV basis); parent-only equity was 8,526 at FY2026.

scenario_narratives.base: Post-Foxtel News Corp is a 5%-growth, ~18-20% margin information and listings group: Dow Jones' B2B data and WSJ subscriptions and the two property portals carry the growth, HarperCollins is a cash cow, News Media is managed for cash through perpetual restructuring. Margin expands ~2.5pp over seven years, roughly half the pace management achieved in FY2026. 38% of the Digital Real Estate profit leaks to REA minorities throughout.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'core growth pillars' deliver: Dow Jones reaches its $1B FY2030 EBITDA target, AI licensing broadens beyond two counterparties, realtor.com closes some of the monetisation gap to Zillow and REA keeps compounding. Margins reach 22.5%. Even so the value is bounded by the minority leakage on the fastest-growing piece and an 18x exit cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Secular print decline, AI traffic disintermediation without durable licensing income, and a housing downturn in both portal markets arrive together; growth stalls near 1.5%, margins drift down to 16.5%, and the dual-class discount persists (12x cap).

valuation_philosophy.summary: A consolidated owner-FCF DCF on continuing operations, with SBC expensed and the share count flat, recurring restructuring charged as a real cost, and the REA Group minority charged once through a tax-plus-leakage driver (so the value is attributable to News Corp shareholders). The headline is what the group's own cash flows are worth at a 9% WACC; it does NOT mark the 62% REA stake to REA's ASX price. Sum-of-parts memo for the reader: at REA.AX A$154.67 (2026-10-02, AUDUSD 0.6928) News Corp's 62% of REA is worth ~US$8.9B (~$16/share) before any holding-company discount, so the market price of ~$28-29 implies ~US$6-7B (~5-6x FY2026 segment EBITDA of ~$1.0B) for Dow Jones + HarperCollins + News Media + Move + corporate, net of cash and investments. The DCF value below the market price therefore says: the stock is only cheap if you believe REA deserves its ~30x earnings market multiple and that it can be realised (spin, sale or collapse of the dual-class structure); on the group's own discounted cash flows it is fully priced.
key_risks_to_valuation: REA Group market multiple vs DCF multiple: the single largest swing. Marking the 38% minority at market instead of at the DCF's own value would lower intrinsic value; marking the 62% stake at market (SOTP) would raise it well above the house number.
Housing cyclicality: Digital Real Estate Services is 46% of segment EBITDA and tied to listings volumes in Australia and the US, both interest-rate sensitive.
AI disintermediation vs AI licensing: OpenAI (~$250M/5yr) and Meta (up to $50M/yr) are fixed-term; non-renewal plus traffic loss is the bear axis.
Structural print decline in News Media (~25% of revenue, ~6% margin) and whether restructuring charges ever stop recurring (the model assumes they do not).

Governance: dual-class structure with ~41% Murdoch voting power on ~14% economic interest; Starboard's proposal to collapse it is non-binding. A persistent conglomerate/governance discount is why the exit cap is 15x rather than 20x.
FX: AUD and GBP earnings translated to USD; a 10% AUD move shifts roughly 2-3% of group EBITDA.

Capital allocation: $1B buyback program and M&A (122 of acquisitions in FY2026); the flat share count assumes buybacks only offset SBC, so incremental repurchases below intrinsic value are upside not modelled.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 22.20-31.66. REA.AX and AUDUSD=X from the same endpoint on 2026-10-02 for the NCI market-value memo.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1564708) and the FY2026 Form 10-K (nws-20260630.htm, filed 2026-08-07): continuing-ops OCF 1,237, capex 426, D&A 485, SBC 77, restructuring 86, cash taxes 272, NCI 170 of 743 continuing NI, debt 1,989 / cash 2,095 at 2026-06-30, investments 1,002 (Note 6), operating lease liability 926, segment table (Dow Jones 2,497/663; Digital Real Estate 2,016/741; Books 2,288/287; News Media 2,227/139; Other -/-203), cover-page shares at 2026-07-31, REA 62.0% / Move 80%. NWSA_Metrics.csv (82 periods) for history.
data_sources.qualitative: NWSA_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): segment mix, Foxtel divestiture, AI licensing deals, Dow Jones FY2030 target, governance and bull/bear axes.

inputs.share_count_basis: 541.05M basic (360,503,747 Class A + 180,548,891 Class B as of 2026-07-31, FY2026 10-K cover) plus 1.9M dilutive RSU/PSU (FY2026 diluted 558.4M less basic 556.5M weighted) = 543.0M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. The company is an active repurchaser ($641M FY2026, new $1B program from July 2025) so the flat count is funded.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation absent from companyfacts; CSV StockBasedComp 77). No separate equity-award tax-withholding line is disclosed, so the figure is the add-back only.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: reported_fcf = continuing-operations OCF 1,237 less capex 426 (FY2026 10-K; discontinued Foxtel OCF of -6 excluded). last_fcf = 811 - 77 SBC = 734 (pre-NCI, after +29 net interest income). Interest income is NOT stripped: net cash is only $106M against a ~$880M unlevered FCF base (far below the 1x materiality threshold); the +29 net interest line is the yield on $2.1B gross cash roughly offsetting the coupon on $2.0B of notes, and both are captured by net_debt in the bridge. The forward build is unlevered from EBITDA components, so last_fcf is a historical anchor, not the projection base.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows: REA Group is 62.0% owned (FY2026 10-K), so 38.0% of its profit leaks to minorities. NCI took 170 of 743 continuing net income in FY2026 (22.9%; 25.9% FY2025, 29.0% FY2024 - falling as Dow Jones outgrew REA). Folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax-plus-leakage driver: 1 - (1-0.27)x(1-0.23) = 43.8%, drifting to 44.5% (base) as the faster-growing REA raises its share of group profit. NCI's share of the small D&A-less-capex add-back (~$14M) is ignored. NOT deducted again in the bridge. Calibration: FY2026 EBIT (1,627 + 77 - 86 - 485 = 1,133) x (1 - 0.438) = 637 vs attributable continuing NI 573 + ~65 after-tax net interest/other = ~638. Memo: at REA.AX A$154.67 (2026-10-02, ~132.1M REA shares, AUDUSD 0.6928) the 38% minority is worth ~US$5.5B at market, more than this DCF implicitly assigns it - see valuation_philosophy.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases ($926M liability at 2026-06-30): lease cost ($165M FY2026) is already inside operating expenses and therefore inside Segment EBITDA, so no lease charge is added to the flows (lease_cost_pct_path omitted) and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Finance leases are nil. One treatment, consistently.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows (with AUD/GBP translation exposure inside them). Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), beta ~1.05, ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% on $2.0B senior notes, ~3.9% after tax; E/V ~89%, D/V ~11% -> ~8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality (housing, advertising), News Media decline, AI disintermediation and governance are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: ebitda_margin_path is pre-SBC and net of recurring restructuring. FY2026 anchor: Total Segment EBITDA 1,627 (already after SBC) + SBC 77 - restructuring charges 86 = 1,618 = 17.9% of revenue (FY2025: 1,415 + 84 - 120 = 16.2%). Restructuring (mostly News Media severance) has recurred every year for a decade (94/120/86 in FY2024-26) and is cash, so Segment EBITDA overstates owner earnings by ~1pp; the paths carry that ~0.9-1.0pp drag permanently. Non-cash impairments (27 in FY2026) are excluded.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company; adaptations file applied for NCI, leases and non-operating assets). News Corp is NOT a holdco of financial assets - it consolidates and operates Dow Jones, HarperCollins, News Media and Move, and controls REA - so the holdco/BVPS row does not apply; the one straddle (the listed 38% REA minority) is handled by the adaptations' charge-once NCI rule rather than a separate sum-of-parts, with the market-value SOTP reported as a memo. FY2026 is the first clean post-Foxtel year (sale to DAZN closed 2025-04-02; Foxtel is discontinued ops in all periods shown, so FY2025 net income of 1,340 includes a 692 gain/disc-ops result). Horizon 10 years because margins are still ramping (management expects further expansion; Dow Jones $1B EBITDA target for FY2030). D&A (5.4%) converges to capex (4.5%) by year 10 so no acquired-intangible amortisation shield is perpetuated. Working capital capture 0: deferred revenue grew only $45M on $576M of revenue growth and HarperCollins carries receivables/inventory, so the net is ~zero. The dcf-context header reads 'FY end ?' because research/NWSA/info.json lacks fiscal_year_end; it is 30 June.

bear.cash_tax_rate_note: Same 27% tax; NCI leakage held at 23% (a housing downturn hits REA and the rest of the group together).
bear.narrative: AI answer-engines erode referral traffic faster than licensing replaces it and the OpenAI/Meta deals are not renewed at the same terms; print decline accelerates and News Media margins thin further despite restructuring; a US/Australian housing downturn cuts listings volumes at realtor.com and REA, with Zillow pressing its audience lead; HarperCollins ex-growth. Revenue ~1.5%/yr, margin slips to 16.5%, restructuring never stops. Governance (dual-class, Murdoch succession) keeps the exit multiple low: 12x cap.

base.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined driver: 27% cash tax on unlevered EBIT (FY2026 cash taxes 272 = 24% of 1,133 EBIT; GAAP 29%; US/AU/UK blend) then 23% NCI leakage rising to 24% as REA's profit share grows.
base.narrative: Dow Jones compounds at 6-7% EBITDA growth toward (but short of) the $1B FY2030 target; Digital Real Estate grows high-single to low-double digits with REA pricing and realtor.com share gains partly offset by housing cyclicality; HarperCollins flat-to-low growth; News Media revenue flat with print decline offset by digital, licensing and cost cuts. Group revenue 5% decaying to 2.5%; pre-SBC margin net of restructuring rises from 17.9% to 20.5% by FY2033 and holds. Terminal 15x owner FCF (Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x; the cap binds).

bull.cash_tax_rate_note: Same 27% tax; NCI leakage drifts to 25% because the bull case is led by REA (38% minority-owned), so more of the upside leaks.
bull.narrative: Dow Jones hits $1B segment EBITDA by FY2030 on Risk & Compliance and B2B data; further AI-licensing deals beyond OpenAI/Meta add a near-100%-margin stream; realtor.com keeps taking share and turns into a meaningful profit contributor; REA sustains double-digit yield growth; News Media stabilises with digital subscriptions and the California Post. Revenue 7% decaying to 3%; margin 22.5% by FY2033. Does NOT include a REA-stake realisation or collapse of the dual-class structure - the SOTP-at-market memo covers that.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the News Media segment is in structural decline, AI disintermediation of discovery traffic is a live and unquantified threat, ~45% of segment EBITDA is housing-cycle-exposed, and the dual-class/Murdoch-succession overhang is a permanent governance discount. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (Dow Jones $1B, realtor.com share gains against Zillow, continued REA pricing, AI-deal renewals). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
